topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) fit
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Mei (Redwood SE), Arjun, Leah, Darren, Priya (Velora)

00:00 - Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really excited to chat through Velora's, your onramp plan to, uh, ship chat and recommendation features. can we do a quick round and goals for today?
00:12 - Arjun: yeah sure i'm arjun, head of product. we've got a short window so main goal is to understand how fast we can get a prototype up and running and what the tradeoffs are between using hosted API vs, um, going dedicated or private. also security is a must.
00:25 - Leah: hi i'm leah, ml eng, i'll be doing the integration work, want to know how long to first call and what tooling we get.
00:33 - Darren: darren, devops, curious about vpc routing and k8s side if we go private.
00:38 - Priya: priya in security — SOC2 questions, key management, and audit logs.
00:45 - Samira: great, thanks. quick context from our side — redwood offers a hosted API that most teams use to get to first token in minutes, we also have Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) options for regulated workloads. today we'll map your constraints to a path and outline a pilot.
01:05 - Jonah: i'll do a short technical sketch — latency/cost expectations and what the quickstart actually looks like.

01:22 - Arjun: high level constraints: user-facing recommendation API at peak ~200 QPS, p95 latency target around 160-200 ms, budget sensitivity — need to keep inference cost predictably low, and data residency — eu-west and us-east but primary is eu. timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, pilot in 6.
01:45 - Samira: ok that's helpful; two-week proto is friendly to hosted, we can get you a trial org, credits, walk-through of SDKs and a sample app. the dedicated option is good later if you need predictable throughput and the private control plane if the compliance team requires VPC-only.
02:03 - Leah: when you say "time-to-first-token" what's realistic? can leah get a curl call now?
02:09 - Jonah: yes, typically 10-30 minutes to a first successful request for a simple text/generate call: sign up, get an API key, run the SDK example. if you want to include streaming or function-calling, add maybe another hour to wire callbacks.
02:27 - Leah: ok that's great. in practice we also want to test latency at 200 qps, is that doable on the hosted trial?
02:34 - Jonah: for a scaled 200 QPS benchmark we usually recommend a short dedicated pilot, but for initial profiling we can run a smoke benchmark on hosted limited to ramping traffic — it won't reflect dedicated tail latencies but you'll get throughput and token cost numbers. we can also provide model variants that are latency-optimized vs cost-optimized.

03:02 - Priya: on security — does hosted keep raw inputs? how long are logs retained by default?
03:09 - Samira: hosted stores request logs for 30 days by default, and we can opt into shorter retention. we also offer an enterprise package with log export, audit logs, and optional private deployments. we integrate with customer KMS for private stacks; for hosted we provide field-level encryption and customer-controlled deletion APIs.
03:29 - Priya: ok what about SOC2 and encryption at rest?
03:33 - Mei: we are SOC2 compliant for our enterprise tiers; keys at rest are managed and we can integrate with your KMS when on Private. we'll share the security pack pdf after this call.

03:50 - Darren: for private deployment, do you provide a helm chart or an appliance? darren: we run strict k8s and ip allow lists.
03:59 - Jonah: we have a private on-prem package and a VPC control-plane option. for VPC we provide an operator and terraform modules; for on-prem there's a packaged runtime and a management agent. routing is via private peering or customer-managed VPN. some of the customers we work with bring their own infra and we ship a chart.

04:25 - Arjun: what's the expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we are price sensitive.
04:31 - Samira: depends heavily on model size and usage pattern. as a rule of thumb hosted is lower friction but slightly higher per-token unit cost; Dedicated reduces unit cost for sustained throughput via reserved capacity. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quant profiles that reduce per-token cost by 20-45% depending on workload. we'll include a cost model spreadsheet.

05:00 - Leah: about models — are there curated models you recommend for recommendation text? we want deterministic-ish outputs and low latency.
05:07 - Jonah: yes, we have a catalog of verified models. for recommendation ranking and short generation we often recommend smaller quantized encoder-decoder or transformer models tuned for latency. we'll propose two variants in the benchmark pack: a low-latency 8-bit quantized variant and a higher-quality float16 candidate.

05:35 - (small crosstalk)
05:42 - Priya: question — audit logs for who called what — is that per-token level or per-request?
05:48 - Mei: audit logs are per-request with metadata; payload retention is configurable. in enterprise private you can route logs to your splunk or cloud logging account.

06:05 - Arjun: ok, let's talk specifics for the trial. we need a playbook: how many credits, what sample prompts, and what success criteria do you recommend?
06:15 - Samira: suggested playbook: we allocate 50k token-equivalent credits to your team for a two-week sandbox. steps: 1) sign up + API key, 2) run quickstart app (we'll give a repo), 3) run our sample benchmark (we provide a JMeter/goreq script), 4) share results and we'll do a guided analysis. success criteria: functional POC, p95 under 250ms on selected model at ramped loads, and cost per request below your threshold (we'll compute).
06:45 - Leah: 50k tokens — is that enough to run the benchmark?
06:49 - Jonah: for an initial functional benchmark yes; if you want sustained 200 QPS tests we'll allocate a separate benchmark window or suggest a short reserved pilot.

07:05 - Darren: needs for network: can we test from our eu nodes only so data doesn't leave region?
07:11 - Mei: yes, we have region routing, and for hosted you can pin regioned endpoints; for compliance we can ensure eu-only processing via our eu-region hosted endpoints or by moving to private.

07:28 - Priya: you mentioned key management for hosted — how does that work? can you give an example?
07:33 - Mei: for hosted we do envelope encryption and can integrate with an external KMS for key wrapping in enterprise agreements. for full control you pick private and we integrate directly with your KMS/HSM.

07:48 - Arjun: ok, final — who will own set up and what are the next milestones?
07:53 - Samira: we'll own the onboarding — i'll create the trial org, credit allotment, and send a quickstart repo link. jonah will send the benchmark pack and sample prompts. we agreed benchmark call next week.

08:10 - Leah: one more practical — do you have SDKs for go and node?
08:14 - Jonah: yes official sdks for node, python, go, and a curl example. we'll include snippets in the quickstart repo.

08:25 - (small typing/interruptions)
08:32 - Priya: i'll email our compliance checklist to samira, can you confirm you'll map items to your security pack?
08:38 - Samira: yes we'll map and follow up.

08:45 - (wrap)
08:47 - Samira: recap: 1) Samira -> trial org + 50k credit by 2/19, 2) Jonah -> benchmark scripts + model recommendations by 2/20, 3) Velora -> send compliance checklist by 2/19, 4) schedule benchmark run for week of 2/23. any other items?
08:58 - Arjun: no, that's it — excited to move fast. thanks everyone.
09:03 - meeting end

Notes on transcript imperfections: some named products mis-stated (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "kay vee cash" in a few places), filler words present, occasional speaker label swaps (e.g., "Mei" sometimes labeled as "Jonah" in the recording).
